# Voiceover script

The complete narration, 5,441 words, about 36 minutes at 150 words a minute. Read it in a professional, friendly tone, a little slower than conversation. Leave a breath of about two seconds between scenes, and three seconds at each chapter card.

Recording tips: one take per scene, named after the scene number (for example `03.2.wav`), so each take lines up with its clip.

## Chapter 1 — Welcome to WorkPulse

**[01.1] Opening** *(28 s)*

Welcome to WorkPulse. Track, focus, achieve. In this tutorial you will learn how to use WorkPulse from beginning to end: setting up your organization, inviting your team, tracking time with the desktop app, approving timesheets, billing your clients, running payroll, and getting the reports you need. Everything you see is the real application, running with a demo company called Northwind Creative, so you can follow along step by step.

**[01.2] Who uses which app** *(41 s)*

WorkPulse has three kinds of users. Administrators and managers use this web app to organize people and projects, approve time, and handle billing and payroll. Workers, the people whose time is tracked, use the WorkPulse desktop app on Windows, macOS or Linux. It tracks their time and shows them their own timesheet, time off and pay stubs. And your clients can get a read-only client portal that shows the work done for them, without any money. What each person sees depends on their role, so two people can see different menus. That is normal, and we will come back to it later.

**[01.3] How this tutorial is organized** *(28 s)*

The menu on the left follows the way work flows through WorkPulse. You set up the organization and invite people. You organize the work into clients, projects and tasks. Your team tracks time. Managers review and approve it. Approved time becomes invoices and payroll. And reports turn it all into insight. This tutorial follows the same order, and the chapter list in the description lets you jump to any part.

## Chapter 2 — Getting started: sign up, sign in and stay secure

**[02.1] Create your organization** *(42 s)*

To start using WorkPulse, create your organization. Enter your name, the name of your company, your work email and a password of at least ten characters. Then click Create organization. You are the owner of this new organization, and WorkPulse takes you straight to the Overview. For a new organization, the Overview shows a Getting started checklist with five steps: invite your team, create a project, set pay and bill rates, connect the desktop app, and review what is tracked. Each step links to the right page, and it ticks itself off as you go. You can hide the checklist at any time.

**[02.2] Sign in and reset a forgotten password** *(34 s)*

Next time, sign in from the Welcome Back page. If you forget your password, click Forgot password, enter your work email and click Send reset link. WorkPulse emails you a link to choose a new password. For your privacy, the message is the same whether or not the address has an account. Back on the sign-in page, enter your email and password. The eye button shows the password so you can check it. Click Sign in, and WorkPulse opens the organization you used last.

**[02.3] Join from an invitation** *(28 s)*

When someone invites you to their organization, you receive an invitation link. Opening it shows this page. Check your name, choose a password and click Join organization. Managers and administrators land in the web app, ready to work. Workers are taken to a page where they download the desktop app instead, because that is where they track their time. You will see that page in the desktop chapter.

**[02.4] Turn on two-factor sign-in** *(45 s)*

Protect your account with two-factor sign-in. Open the account menu, choose Profile and devices, and find Two-factor authentication. Click Set up and confirm your password. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator, then type the six-digit code it shows and click Turn on. WorkPulse now gives you ten recovery codes. Each one works once, if you ever lose your phone. Download them and keep them somewhere safe, tick the box and click Done. From now on, signing in asks for a code from your phone. Administrators can also require two-factor for everyone, which we will see in the security chapter.

## Chapter 3 — Finding your way around

**[03.1] The Overview dashboard** *(42 s)*

The Overview is your home page. It updates live, so you always see the current picture. At the top, This month shows the time logged, the estimated pay, the billable time and the estimated amount to bill. Estimates come from your rates and become final once the time is approved. Worked today shows how much your team has tracked so far today. Waiting for approval counts the timesheets and manual time requests that need your decision, and Project budgets warns you before a project runs over. The switch at the top right changes whose numbers you see: everyone, only yourself, or one member.

**[03.2] Customize the Overview** *(36 s)*

You can arrange the Overview to suit the way you work. Click Customize. Every card now has controls to change its size, move it up or down, or hide it. Hidden cards wait in the Hidden widgets panel, so you can add them back at any time. There are cards for the current timer, who is working, recent screenshots, time off, attendance, invoices, weekly limits and more. When you are happy with the layout, click Save layout. Each person has their own layout, and Reset brings back the default.

**[03.3] Menu, organizations, notifications and your account** *(41 s)*

The sidebar groups the pages by job: Time Tracking, Workforce, Project Management, Finance and Reports, with Settings and Help at the bottom. Click a group to open it. At the top left is the organization switcher. If you belong to more than one organization, switch between them here, or create a new one. At the top right, the bell shows your notifications, such as a timesheet waiting for approval or a time off request. Click Mark all read to clear them. Next to it is your account menu, with your profile and devices, what is monitored, and the light and dark themes.

**[03.4] The Help Center and the product tour** *(40 s)*

Whenever you are unsure, open Help. The Help Center is a plain-language manual for the whole app. Search for what you want to do, for example invoice, and open a guide. Each guide gives you numbered steps, with buttons that take you straight to the right page. Many pages also have their own Help link at the top. If you are new, click Start the tour. It highlights each part of the screen with a short explanation. Use Next to move on, or Skip tour to close it. The tour starts by itself the first time you sign in.

## Chapter 4 — Set up your organization

**[04.1] Organization settings** *(32 s)*

Now let us set up the organization. Open Settings. The tabs across the top hold every setting, and you only see the ones your role allows. On the Organization tab, the General panel sets your company name, time zone, the day your week starts, your currency, and how durations are shown. The Company profile below holds your logo, tax ID, address and contact details. They appear on your invoices and pay stubs. After a change, click Save changes.

**[04.2] Time & pay: periods, rules, overtime and break types** *(46 s)*

The Time and pay tab controls how time becomes pay. The timesheet period sets how often members submit their time, for example every week. Timesheet rules can lock old time so it cannot be changed, set minimum hours, and remind people about missing time. Below are the overtime rules and your time types, such as regular or overtime, each with its own pay and bill multiplier. Break types define the breaks your people can take. Let us add a coffee break: name it Coffee, make it a paid break, with a maximum of fifteen minutes. And a lunch break: unpaid, up to sixty minutes. We will plan these breaks on a project in a moment.

**[04.3] Choose what the desktop app tracks** *(44 s)*

Tracking policies decide what the desktop app records. The organization default applies to everyone. Activity counts keyboard and mouse use, never the keys themselves. Idle detection asks people what to do with time when they step away. Screenshots can be switched on, taken a set number of times every ten minutes, and blurred. Apps and URLs record which applications and websites are used. You can override any setting for a team or for one member. Here, the Client Success team has its screenshots blurred. An overridden setting shows Reset to inherited. When you save, the affected members are notified, and each member can always see what is monitored.

**[04.4] Roles and permissions** *(34 s)*

Roles control who can see and do what. WorkPulse comes with built-in roles: System Admin for full access, Team Manager for running teams and projects without the money settings, and Worker for people who track time. The matrix shows every permission for every role. If you need something in between, create a custom role. Give it a name, start from an existing role, and then adjust its permissions. Each permission can apply to the person themselves, their assigned projects, their team, or the whole organization.

## Chapter 5 — Add your people

**[05.1] Invite a member** *(35 s)*

To add people, open Workforce, then Members, and click Invite member. Enter their email address and name, and choose a role. Most people you track are Workers. You can also put them in teams and give them projects right away, so everything is ready when they join. Click Send invitation. WorkPulse emails the invitation. If the email cannot be sent, the dialog shows the invitation link so you can share it yourself. Until the person accepts, the invitation waits under Pending invitations, where you can revoke it.

**[05.2] A member’s profile** *(29 s)*

Click a member to open their profile. The Overview shows their details, quick links and access. Here you can suspend or remove someone, or reset their two-factor sign-in if they lose their phone. Personal info holds HR details and private notes. The other tabs show the member's time, activity, projects, the computers they use, and the tracking policy that applies to them, combined from the organization, their team and any personal overrides.

**[05.3] Create a team and choose its manager** *(30 s)*

Teams group people who work together. On the Teams tab, click New team, give it a name and a description, and click Create team. Then add people. A team member with the Manager role approves the team's timesheets and time off, and sees the team's time and activity. Here, Priya becomes the manager of the new Video Production team, and Kenji joins as a member. A person can belong to more than one team.

## Chapter 6 — Clients, projects and tasks

**[06.1] Add a client** *(30 s)*

Work in WorkPulse is organized into clients, projects and tasks. Start with the client. Open Project Management, then Clients, and click New client. Enter the company name and a contact person. The contact email is where invoices are sent. Choose the client's currency, and if you charge this client a standard hourly rate, enter it here. You can also add a logo, a colour and the language for documents such as invoices. Click Create client.

**[06.2] Delete a client created by mistake, or archive one** *(39 s)*

Sometimes a client is created by mistake, for example twice. A client that was never used can be deleted. Open its actions menu and choose Delete. WorkPulse explains what will be removed: the client with its projects, tasks, rates, budgets and portal access. Deleting only works for a client with no invoices, payments, expenses or tracked time, and it cannot be undone. For a client you have worked with, use Archive instead. Archiving hides the client and its projects but keeps all its history, and you can restore it later. Tick Show archived to see archived clients.

**[06.3] Share a client portal** *(34 s)*

Clients can follow the work you do for them in a client portal. From the client's actions, open Client portal. Switch the portal on and choose what the client sees: hours per person, task and day, task progress and hour budgets, activity levels, and even screenshots taken on their projects. The portal never shows money. Click Preview as client to see exactly what they will see. To give someone access, enter their email and click Invite. You can revoke access at any time.

**[06.4] Create a project** *(35 s)*

Next, create a project for the client. Open Projects and click New project. Give it a name and choose the client. Add start and end dates and an estimate of the hours, so WorkPulse can show progress against the plan. Then choose who works on it, either individual members or whole teams. Members only see and track the projects they are assigned to. In the finance section you can set pay and bill rates for this project, or mark it as not billable. Click Create project.

**[06.5] Plan breaks for a project** *(34 s)*

For projects with a regular rhythm, you can plan breaks. Open the project and go to its Settings tab. In the Breaks section, click Add break, choose a break type and, if you like, a time and a length. Here we plan a fifteen minute coffee break at ten thirty, and an hour for lunch at twelve. Click Save changes. People on this project now see these breaks as one-tap buttons in the desktop app, with a reminder when a break is due.

**[06.6] Add tasks** *(31 s)*

Tasks break a project into pieces of work. Open Tasks and click New task. Choose the project, give the task a title, and set its status, priority, due date and an estimate in hours. Assign it to one or more people. When they track time, they can pick the task, so you see exactly where the hours went. Filter the list by project or status, or switch on Assigned to me to see your own work.

## Chapter 7 — The desktop app for workers

**[07.1] Download and install the desktop app** *(36 s)*

Now let us switch to the worker's side. Workers use WorkPulse through the desktop app. After accepting an invitation, they land on this download page. It offers the right installer for their computer: Windows, macOS, or Ubuntu and Debian. Click the download button. A short guide opens with the install steps, and a link to the full setup guide with a picture for each step. On Windows, for example, if Windows protects your PC, click More info and then Run anyway. The app updates itself automatically from then on.

**[07.2] Sign in to the desktop app** *(30 s)*

Open WorkPulse on your computer and sign in with the same email and password you use for WorkPulse. You can also sign in through your browser instead. If your organization requires it, an administrator approves new computers before they can track time. Once you are signed in, the menu on the left takes you to everything you need: Home, Track, Timesheet, Time off, Schedule, Pay stubs and Settings. The app only shows your own data.

**[07.3] Clock in** *(43 s)*

This is Home. To start work, choose a project. The timer starts right away and the status changes to Clocked in. You can also choose a task, and change project at any time with the Change button. Below the timer are the breaks planned for this project, the ones we set up earlier, ready as one-tap buttons. Add a short work note so your manager knows what you are working on. On the right, Today's summary shows your tracked time today and this week, how much was active, and your shift. If your organization records activity, it is shown here too, so nothing is hidden from you.

**[07.4] Breaks and idle time** *(43 s)*

When it is time for a break, tap it. WorkPulse pauses your time and shows how long is left. When a planned break is due, the app reminds you, and if a break runs long, it tells you how far over you are. When you are back, click Clock back in. If you step away from the computer without taking a break, WorkPulse notices that there was no keyboard or mouse activity. When you return, it asks what to do with that time. Keep it if you were working, for example in a meeting, or discard it. If you do not answer, your organization's default applies.

**[07.5] Clock out with an end-of-day report** *(34 s)*

At the end of the day, click Clock out. WorkPulse asks for a short end-of-day report: what you completed, and whether the work is finished. Your manager reads these reports in the web app. The report is saved on your computer first, so it is never lost, even when you are offline. Click Submit and clock out. In fact, if your internet connection drops at any time, the app keeps tracking and sends everything when you are back online. No tracked time is lost.

**[07.6] Projects, tasks, sessions and manual time** *(34 s)*

Track holds your work. Projects lists everything you are assigned to; click one to start tracking it. Tasks shows your tasks, and you can start the timer straight from a task. Sessions lists the time you tracked over the last days. Forgot to start the timer, for example during a call on your phone? Click Add manual time, choose the project and the time, and give a reason. Depending on your organization, manual time is added straight away or sent to your manager for approval.

**[07.7] Your timesheet, activity and reports** *(40 s)*

Timesheet shows your time for the current period, with the hours for each day. Use Previous and Next to look at other periods. When the period is complete, click Submit to send it to your manager for approval. If your manager asks for changes, the timesheet comes back to you and the Home page tells you what needs attention. Activity shows your own activity blocks and the apps and websites that were recorded, exactly what your manager can see. Reports gives you your worked hours by day and by project for this week, last week or this month.

**[07.8] Time off, schedule, pay stubs and settings** *(35 s)*

To ask for time off, open Time off and click Request time off. Choose the type, the dates, and add a reason if you like, then click Send request. Your manager is notified, and you can follow the request here. Schedule shows your working hours for this week and next. Pay stubs lists your pay stubs once payroll is finalized, each one with a PDF to download. Finally, Settings shows who you are signed in as, your organization and this device, and lets you sign out.

## Chapter 8 — Watching the work

**[08.1] Who is working now** *(39 s)*

Back in the web app, let us see the work as it happens. Open Time Tracking, then Live. Who is working now shows everyone's status, updated live: working, idle or paused, or offline, with the project they are on and how long they have been working. Filter by status to focus on one group. From a member's actions you can open their activity or their current session. And if someone forgot to stop their timer, choose Force stop timer. The desktop app stops within about a minute, and the change is recorded in the audit log.

**[08.2] Session history** *(26 s)*

Session history lists every work session: who, on which project and task, where it was tracked from, when it started and ended, and why it ended. Filter by date or member, or search. Click a session to see its details: the time worked, each segment between pauses and breaks, and every change of state. From here you can jump to that day's activity.

**[08.3] Screenshots, apps and websites** *(34 s)*

Activity shows how a day went, in ten-minute blocks. Choose a member and a day. Each block shows the activity level, the share of time with keyboard or mouse use, and the screenshots taken, if your policy records them. Click a block for its details. Use the activity filter to find quiet periods quickly. The Apps and URLs tabs show which applications and websites were used, and for how long. Remember: keystrokes are only counted, never recorded, and members see the same information about themselves.

**[08.4] End-of-day reports** *(32 s)*

Remember the report Ava wrote when she clocked out? Managers read them under End-of-day reports. The summary shows how many reports came in, from how many people, how many marked their work as finished, and the time they cover. Reports are grouped by day. Click one to read it in full, with its session. Previous and Next move through the reports, and Copy report puts the text on your clipboard, for example to paste into a client update.

**[08.5] What is monitored: full transparency** *(23 s)*

Monitoring works best when everyone knows the rules. Every person can open What is monitored from their account menu. It explains in plain language what is recorded while they track time, which limits and time rules apply, and who can see their data. Owners, administrators and managers are not tracked unless you choose to track them.

## Chapter 9 — Time and approvals

**[09.1] Find and correct time entries** *(39 s)*

Time entries is where you find and correct time. Pick a date range, then filter by member, client, project or task, or search. The totals at the bottom show the time logged, billable time, and the estimated pay and billing. To correct an entry, open its actions and choose Edit. Change what you need, and give a reason for the change. Every change is kept: View history shows each revision, who made it and why. You can also split an entry in two, duplicate it, or select several entries to mark them billable or delete them together.

**[09.2] Add time for someone** *(34 s)*

Sometimes time needs to be added by hand, for example a meeting away from the computer. Click Add time, choose the member and the date, and enter either a duration or a start and end time. Choose the project and task, describe the work and give a reason. Depending on your settings, the time goes straight onto the timesheet, or it becomes a manual time request for approval. Members can also import time from a CSV file on their timesheet, using the template provided.

**[09.3] Approve timesheets and manual time** *(38 s)*

When members submit their timesheets, they arrive in Approvals. Click a timesheet to review the days, projects and totals. If everything is right, click Approve. Approved time is final: it is what payroll pays and what invoices bill. If something needs fixing, click Request changes and explain what is wrong. The timesheet goes back to the member as a draft. Reject works the same way. To approve many at once, use the Approve button at the top of the list. Below, manual time requests wait for the same decision: approve or reject each one.

**[09.4] Your team's week** *(20 s)*

Team week gives you the whole team at a glance: the hours each member worked on each day of the week. It is the quickest way to spot missing days before you approve. Move between weeks with the arrows, and select a row to open that member's timesheet.

## Chapter 10 — Schedules, attendance and time off

**[10.1] Working hours** *(28 s)*

Schedules hold everyone's working hours. Open Workforce, then Schedules, to see the week for each member. To change someone's hours, open their schedule. Set the time zone, the date the new hours start, and the start and end for each working day. Saving creates a new version, so past attendance is still measured against the hours that applied at the time. Members see their own schedule in the desktop app.

**[10.2] Attendance** *(23 s)*

Attendance compares the schedule with the time actually tracked. For each person you see whether they are present, late, absent, on leave, on a holiday, or not started yet. Filter by status to follow up quickly, and switch between a single day and the whole week. WorkPulse can also alert managers about late starts and missed shifts.

**[10.3] Approve time off, policies and holidays** *(38 s)*

Time off requests arrive under Time off, on the Requests tab. Here is the request Ava sent from the desktop app. Approve it, or reject it with a comment, and she is notified straight away. The Calendar shows who is away and when. On Policies and holidays you set up the kinds of time off, such as paid time off or sick leave: whether they are paid, whether they need approval, and how much is earned each month. You can adjust a member's balance by hand, and add public holidays, which are paid automatically.

## Chapter 11 — Money: rates, budgets, expenses, invoices and payroll

**[11.1] Pay and bill rates** *(37 s)*

Money in WorkPulse starts with rates. Open Finance, then Rates. Bill rates are what you charge clients per hour. Pay rates are what you pay members per hour. A rate can apply to the whole organization, a client, a project, a member, or a member on one project, and the most specific one wins. Rates are effective-dated: when a rate changes, set the date it starts, and past time keeps its old rate. Here we give the new Lumen project a bill rate of one hundred and twenty-five per hour, from today.

**[11.2] Budgets** *(32 s)*

Budgets warn you before a project or client costs more than planned. Budgets shows how many are healthy, close to the limit, or exceeded. Click Set budget, choose a project or a client, and set the budget in hours or in money. It can run for the whole project or reset every month. Warn at sets when WorkPulse alerts you, for example at eighty percent. The same progress bars appear on the Overview and in the client portal.

**[11.3] Expenses** *(32 s)*

People can submit expenses with a receipt, such as travel or software, and mark them as billable to the client or to be reimbursed. Under Expenses, the Submitted tab holds the ones waiting for a decision. Check the receipt, then approve or reject. Once you have paid someone back, click Reimburse. Approved billable expenses can be added to the client's next invoice. Like every finance list, Expenses has a period filter and an Export button for CSV, Excel or PDF.

**[11.4] Create an invoice** *(39 s)*

Invoices turn billable time into money. The Invoices page shows what is outstanding, what is overdue, your drafts, and what has been collected. Click New invoice. Choose the client and the period to bill, and how to group the time: by project, task or member. You can include approved billable expenses and set a tax rate. Click Preview lines. WorkPulse builds the lines from the billable time and the bill rates, and you can add custom lines too. Then set the issue date, the due date and a note, review the totals, and create the draft invoice.

**[11.5] Send the invoice and record the payment** *(34 s)*

On the invoice, Download PDF gives you the finished document with your logo and the client's details. Click Send to email it to the client's contact; if the client has no email, you can mark it as sent and deliver it yourself. When the client pays, click Record payment. Enter the amount, the date, the method and a reference such as the transfer ID. A payment can also be split across several open invoices. The invoice is now paid, and Payments received lists every payment.

**[11.6] Run payroll** *(36 s)*

Payroll pays your people from approved time. First, pay groups set who is paid together, how often, and in which currency. Then, on the Payrolls tab, click Run payroll, choose the pay group and the period, and create a draft. WorkPulse calculates each person's pay from their approved hours, overtime and paid time off. Each approved hour is paid exactly once. Add bonuses or deductions with Adjust. When everything is right, click Finalize. Finalizing cannot be undone: corrections go on the next payroll. Members can now see their pay stubs.

**[11.7] Pay stubs, paid and owed** *(27 s)*

Each member's pay stub is a PDF. Members also find it in the desktop app, under Pay stubs. Once the money has gone out, click Mark as paid. The Owed tab answers a different question: how much do you owe each member for a period, right now? It shows tracked and approved time, and the estimated and approved amounts. Estimated becomes approved once the timesheets are approved.

## Chapter 12 — Reports

**[12.1] Summary** *(30 s)*

For a quick answer, open Reports, then Summary. It shows the time logged, estimated pay, billable time and estimated billing for a period, together with average activity and days off. Switch between daily, weekly, fortnightly and monthly periods, and step back with the arrows. Below are the hours per day, by client, and by project, and a table with every person's totals. Members who open Summary see only their own time, and never any money.

**[12.2] Run and export a report** *(36 s)*

The Report library is organized by the question you want answered: where did time go, who was late or absent, which timesheets are still pending, what is billable per client, and more. Open a report, for example Time and activity. Filter by date, members, teams, projects or clients, and group the rows by up to three things, such as member, project and client. Export downloads the result as CSV, Excel or PDF. Large reports can be prepared in the background, and you are notified when the file is ready.

**[12.3] Save a report and schedule it by email** *(32 s)*

If you need the same report regularly, save it. Click Save report and give it a name. Choose a relative date range, such as last month, so it always shows fresh numbers, and share it with everyone who can run the report if you like. Switch on Email on a schedule, choose how often and in which format, and add the recipients. WorkPulse now sends the report automatically. Saved reports appear at the top of the Report library.

## Chapter 13 — Security and administration

**[13.1] Devices** *(26 s)*

Settings, Devices lists every computer signed in to the desktop app: whose it is, the operating system, the app version and its status. From a device's actions you can approve it, when your organization requires approval for new computers, ask for a new sign-in, or revoke it, for example when a laptop is lost. A revoked device can no longer send any data.

**[13.2] Sign-in security and access review** *(34 s)*

Under Security and retention you decide how people sign in. Require two-factor authentication for admins only or for everyone, set how long a session lasts, require approval for new devices, and limit sign-in to your office networks with an IP allowlist. The data retention settings decide how long data is kept. Access review then gives you a regular check of who can do what: every active member, who still has no two-factor sign-in, your roles and their permissions, and the active API keys.

**[13.3] Keep screenshots for a set time** *(29 s)*

Screenshots are kept for a set period, thirty days by default, and older ones are deleted automatically on a schedule. Nothing is ever deleted until an administrator previews what would go and approves it. Click Preview cleanup to see how many screenshots would be deleted, then approve the cleanup. If you shorten the period later, the approval is withdrawn and you are asked again. The history below shows every cleanup that ran.

**[13.4] Connect other systems: API keys and webhooks** *(39 s)*

To connect WorkPulse to other systems, such as accounting or HR software, create an API key. Give it a name, choose exactly what it may access, and when it expires. The key is shown only once, so store it safely. Webhooks work the other way around: WorkPulse calls your system when something happens, for example when a timesheet is approved. Add the endpoint address and choose the events. You can leave it switched off until your system is ready. Each delivery is signed with a secret, so your system can check it really comes from WorkPulse.

**[13.5] The audit log** *(30 s)*

Finally, the audit log records every important action: who did what, when, and to what. Earlier we deleted a client; here is that action. Filter by action, by type, or by date, and open an entry to see the details. The log cannot be changed, and you can export it to CSV for your records. And for privacy requests, a member's profile lets you export all of their personal data, or erase it.

## Chapter 14 — The team manager's view

**[14.1] WorkPulse as a team manager** *(38 s)*

Here is the same organization through the eyes of Maya, who manages the Design team. Her Overview shows her team, not the whole company. Her menu is shorter: she can approve her team's timesheets and time off, watch their work, and manage the projects she is assigned to, but she does not see rates, payroll or the organization settings. That is why two people can see different menus, and why a page someone else talks about may be missing for you. If you need access to something, ask an administrator to change your role.

## Chapter 15 — Questions and troubleshooting

**[15.1] Frequently asked questions** *(45 s)*

Let us finish with the questions people ask most, all answered in the Help Center. Why are members sent to a download page? Because workers use the desktop app, not the website. Can approved time still be changed? Yes: reopen the timesheet, correct it and approve it again. Once its time is on an invoice, void the invoice first; once it has been paid, correct it with a bonus or deduction on the next payroll. What happens when a computer is offline? The app keeps tracking and sends everything when it is back online. And are keystrokes recorded? No. WorkPulse only counts keyboard and mouse activity. It never records what you type.

**[15.2] Troubleshooting** *(51 s)*

Troubleshooting covers the usual problems. A member forgot to stop their timer: force stop it from Live, then edit or split the entry in Time entries. A member's time is missing: check that their app is online, since offline time arrives when they reconnect, and that their computer is approved under Devices. For time they really did not track, add manual time. The Approve button is greyed out: time was added after the timesheet was submitted, so click Request changes and approve it once they resubmit. And if a member does not have the latest desktop app: updates download in the background and install when the member quits the app from its icon in the system tray. Each guide links straight to the page that fixes it.

## Chapter 16 — Wrap-up

**[16.1] Recap** *(32 s)*

Let us recap the whole journey. You created your organization and set the rules for time and pay. You invited your people, organized them into teams, and set up clients, projects and tasks. Workers tracked their time with the desktop app, with breaks, idle checks and end-of-day reports. Managers watched the work, corrected time and approved timesheets. And approved time became invoices and payroll, with reports to tell you how it all went. Everything comes together here on the Overview.

**[16.2] Closing** *(16 s)*

Thank you for watching. Whenever you need a reminder, open Help inside WorkPulse: every topic in this video has a step-by-step guide there, and the product tour is one click away. Now it is your turn. Track, focus, achieve.
